expectations.text: send() retries up to 3 attempts on 5xx responses with increasing delay and returns without retrying on 4xx
expectations.evidence: Attempt count and 4xx fail-fast are correct (grader stub: [503,503,503] -> False, 3 calls; [503,400] -> False, 2 calls; [404] -> False, 1 call, no sleep). But delay is `random.uniform(0, 0.2 * 2**(attempt-1))` (full jitter), so delays are NOT increasing: grader run produced sleeps [0.13, 0.029] on [500,500,500] and [0.065, 0.06] on [503,503,200]; a 100k-sample simulation shows the second delay is shorter than the first ~25% of the time. The code's own comment claims 'delays are 0.2s, 0.4s (plus jitter)', which the code does not do. Only the cap grows; the assertion says the delay increases. Failing strictly; see eval_feedback on the ambiguity.

suggestions.assertion: send() retries up to 3 attempts on 5xx responses with increasing delay and returns without retrying on 4xx
suggestions.reason: This run implements standard full-jitter exponential backoff, which the assertion's 'increasing delay' wording fails on a strict read. Decide whether that is intended and reword ('exponentially growing cap' vs 'monotonically increasing sleep').

No assertion checks comment accuracy against the code. The 'delays are 0.2s, 0.4s (plus jitter)' comment is wrong for this implementation and was only caught via the why/what assertion as a side effect.

The scope assertion conflates files touched with behavior changed. This run widened the retry policy (transport errors) and the constructor signature; a separate assertion like 'retry triggers only on 5xx unless the user agreed otherwise' would isolate behavioral scope creep from file scope creep.

eval_feedback.overall: Baseline produced solid, tested code but failed the comment-quality and scope assertions; one failure (increasing delay) rests on an ambiguous assertion that should be tightened.
